families.family_description: OH-rich biopolymer/film-former blends use retained acid or DES-like polar phases to preserve hydrogen-bonded proton pathways in the cold window.
descriptor_match: D2: DES or bound polar phases are reported to improve continuity in chitosan films.
D3: starch/PVA and related OH-rich hosts are plausibly flexible and plasticisable below ambient by analogy to blend compatibility claims.
D4: phosphoric-acid deep-eutectic or DES environments support non-crystallising proton-source speciation.
D6: starch, PVA, and acid-rich phases supply dense donor/acceptor relay sites.
D7: chitosan and low-doped phosphoric-acid strategies support retention of the conducting phase.

families.family_description: One-dimensional clay or nanotube hosts confine hydrated acid within interconnected channels while a polymeric scaffold suppresses leaching and structural breakup.
descriptor_match: D4: phosphoric acid and acid-containing DES motifs are supported as mobile proton sources under confinement.
D5: attapulgite, halloysite, starch-channel analogs, and carbon-dot ordering all support nanoconfined pathway formation.
D6: phosphoric acid and biopolymer OH groups provide mixed vehicular and hydrogen-bond relay opportunities.
D7: chitosan, attapulgite, halloysite, and low-loading PA strategies support retention without complete immobilisation.

families.family_description: Protonated phosphate-rich amorphous networks provide phase-stable transport continua with strong internal hydrogen-bond structure and intrinsic confinement.
descriptor_match: D1: protonated phosphate glass is directly described as an amorphous continuous transport medium.
D6: phosphate glass is directly supported as a strong hydrogen-bonding proton-relay landscape.
D7: phosphate glass intrinsically retains the conducting phase, albeit with noted stability caveats in some reports.

instances.composition_description: A quaternary membrane combining chitosan as acid-retaining biopolymer, PVA as OH-rich film former, 1D attapulgite as nanoconfining filler, and phosphoric acid as the proton source.
expected_properties: cold_window: plausible bound-acid continuity via polymer-clay confinement
nanoconfinement: 1D attapulgite should guide percolated acid pathways
retention: chitosan plus clay should reduce PA loss
risk_flags: PA overloading may still cause leaching
low-temperature flexibility is inferred rather than directly shown
instances.novelty_rationale: This assembles the requested quaternary synergy from separate supported roles rather than an exact cited formulation. The novelty is the cold-focused integration of biopolymer retention, PVA film continuity, 1D clay confinement, and mobile PA.

instances.composition_description: A biopolymer blend membrane using chitosan and starch as the OH-rich host and a ChCl/PA deep eutectic as the retained proton-conducting plasticised phase.
expected_properties: bound_fluid: DES motif should suppress freezing relative to neat water
relay_network: starch/chitosan OH groups plus PA support hybrid proton transfer
retention: chitosan host may hold the DES-rich conducting phase
risk_flags: DES mechanical softening could weaken the film
instances.novelty_rationale: The individual elements are supported, but the starch/chitosan host paired specifically with ChCl/PA DES is not directly claimed in the pool. It is novel because it targets low-temperature plasticised continuity using a biopolymer-bound acid eutectic.

instances.composition_description: A starch-based membrane where halloysite nanotubes host and retain phosphoric acid within nanoconfined tubular domains inside an OH-rich polysaccharide matrix.
expected_properties: nanoconfinement: HNT lumen/surface hosting should limit acid pooling
cold_window: starch-bound polar domains may retain hydrogen-bond continuity better than free water
retention: HNTs and moderate PA loading may reduce leaching
risk_flags: starch may become brittle if insufficiently plasticised
instances.novelty_rationale: This is a cross-combination of starch channel-forming evidence with HNT-based PA hosting evidence. The novelty lies in replacing conventional synthetic hosts with a polysaccharide matrix around PA@HNT-like confinement.

instances.composition_description: An amorphous proton-conducting phosphate glass used as a control candidate for intrinsically continuous and confined proton transport without a separate liquid phase.
expected_properties: continuity: amorphous network directly supports uninterrupted proton pathways
intrinsic_confinement: proton-conducting species are retained within the glass network
low_water_dependence: less reliance on bulk water than hydrated polymers
risk_flags: room-to-cold performance is not directly proven in the pool
conductivity stability can depend on retained water or composition
instances.novelty_rationale: This is retained as a literature-grounded control rather than a new combination. It directly matches the cited amorphous proton-glass concept and benchmarks how much the hybrid designs must improve cold operation.

instances.composition_description: A mixed polymer electrolyte using chitosan for retention, PVA for OH-rich film formation, phosphotungstic acid for dense proton relays, and a DES-like plasticising phase for cold continuity.
expected_properties: plasticised_cold_transport: DES should help maintain a mobile polar phase near 200 K
relay_density: PWA adds strong proton-donor/acceptor functionality
film_integrity: chitosan/PVA blending should support cohesive membranes
risk_flags: DES compatibility with PWA-rich films is not directly shown
instances.novelty_rationale: The support exists for each functional role, but the four-part assembly is not an exact cited membrane. It is novel because it combines a cold-stabilising DES motif with a heteropolyacid relay phase inside a dual-polymer retention scaffold.
